# /handoff — consolidated fresh start

Evidence: once a session takes a wrong turn, models do not recover by continuing — external consolidation restores performance (F5); small focused prompts beat full long histories (F9). This command is that consolidation step.

## Step 1 — Verify state against ground truth FIRST

Read `.governor/ledger.md` (the running ledger — goal, decisions, ruled-out) and `.governor/session-facts.log` (the auto-captured factual arc) as your starting material — much of the brief is already there. Then establish what is actually true right now. Run the checks that apply to the current work (do not skip this — a brief built from memory propagates content rot, F10):

- `git status` and `git diff --stat` if in a repo
- The relevant test command(s) if code was touched
- Re-read any file whose content you are about to summarize, if you last saw it many turns ago

Mark every claim in the brief as **verified** (you just checked it) or **unverified** (from session memory).

## Step 2 — Write the brief

Write to `.governor/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<short-slug>.md` (create dirs as needed) with exactly these sections:

```markdown
# Handoff: <one-line title>

## Goal
<what this work stream is trying to achieve — one or two sentences>

## Current state (verified against ground truth)
<bullet list; each bullet tagged [verified] or [unverified]>

## Decisions + why
<bullet list; decision — rationale>

## Failure lessons
<one line each: "tried X, failed because Y" — record the lesson, DROP the details (F10: dead ends are distractors)>

## Contradicted claims (proven false — do not relearn)
<one line each: claims this session DISPROVEN, e.g. "the bug is NOT in the parser — ruled out by test Z". Current models tend to defend a wrong claim established early; naming the disproven claim stops the next session relearning it (F10 + anti-poisoning heuristic)>

## Next steps
<ordered, concrete, smallest-first>

## Files touched
<paths>

## Commands to re-verify
<exact single-line commands the next session should run before trusting this brief>
```

Keep it tight: the target is a brief a fresh session can act on in one read (F9: ~300 focused tokens beat ~113K of history). Do not paste transcripts, logs, or dead-end details into it.

## Step 3 — Hand off

Tell the user: the brief is written; run `/clear` — the next session will be offered the brief automatically by the context-governor SessionStart hook.
